confusion_matrix_note: rows: true state, columns: predicted state, in the order of `labels`; counts of 60 s windows
pvt_correlation_note: Spearman correlation, over the 36 DROZY tests (one point per test), between the shipped model's mean fatigueScore and the test's mean PVT reaction time; positive = the score rises as reactions slow down. Nothing is fitted on DROZY. Details and baselines in `drozy_validation`. DROZY: Massoz, Langohr, François & Verly (2016), The ULg Multimodality Drowsiness Database (called DROZY) and Examples of Use, WACV 2016.
auc_definition: macro average of the three one-vs-rest AUCs, on pooled out-of-fold windows

validation.inner: C from [0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0] by lowest pooled log loss over 5 subject-grouped folds of the training subjects
validation.correlated_windows: Windows of a video overlap by 50 s and share one label: the window counts overstate the evidence. Intervals resample the subjects, not the windows.

chosen.how: Product decision of the team, taken after seeing the four-way comparison, the fold-internal selection and the calibration sensitivity reported here: ship eye closure `blendshape` with `absolute` features, which is what faceWorker.ts already computes and needs no calibration. Reasons: it does not depend on how a session starts, and it is the only variant whose evaluation does not depend on a calibration recording. It is a fixed setting of the pipeline, not a selection on test folds.

secondary_analyses: `configurations` (the shipped one and three alternatives on the same windows), `nested_selection` and `calibration_sensitivity` are secondary. The decision in `chosen.how` was taken after seeing them.

nested_selection.note: Secondary analysis, not the shipped model. If the configuration were chosen by a score, the honest way is inside every fold from the training subjects alone (inner AUC); this is what that procedure scores.

calibration_sensitivity.question: ear_p80 takes its eye threshold from the first 120 s of the person's ALERT video. What if it comes from the first 120 s of the video being scored, whatever state the person is in?
calibration_sensitivity.how: The out-of-fold `ear_p80/absolute` models, unchanged (trained with the alert-video threshold); only the test subject's windows are recomputed with a threshold from each video's own first 120 s. Both versions are scored on the same windows: those that touch the first 120 s of no video.

calibrated_features.what: The same question for the `calibrated` features: the out-of-fold `blendshape/calibrated` models, unchanged, with the test subject's reference taken from the first 120 s of each video instead of the alert video.

calibration_sensitivity.reading: RLDD has no recording that starts rested and then turns drowsy, so neither version is the product's case. The alert-video threshold assumes the calibration was taken rested; the scored-video threshold is what happens when the session starts with the person already in the state being measured.

baseline.formula: clamp01(0.6 * perclos + 0.25 * min(1, yawnsPerMin / 4) + 0.15 * clamp01(12 * std(noseY)))
baseline.what: faceWorker.ts today: blendshape PERCLOS of the last minute, streaming yawn count, spread of the nose height over the last 90 frames

as_three_class_model.how: the formula's number as the only feature of the same logistic regression, in the same folds: the best three-way split that number allows

model.rule: a video gets the class most of its windows got; ties go to the class with the higher mean probability

baseline_as_three_class_model.rule: a video gets the class most of its windows got; ties go to the class with the higher mean probability

final_model.note: refit on every subject; the metrics in this file are out of fold, not of this refit

definitions.perclos: closed frames / frames with a face, in the window
definitions.blink_rate_per_min: eye closures shorter than 0.5 s, per observed minute
definitions.mean_blink_duration_s: mean duration of those short closures (last closed frame - first + one frame period); missing when there is none
definitions.long_closure_rate_per_min: eye closures of 0.5 s or more, per observed minute (assumption: the 0.5 s boundary)
definitions.yawns_per_min: yawns found in the window by the YawDD-calibrated detector (yawn_params.json), per window minute
definitions.head_pitch_std_deg: population standard deviation of the head pitch (degrees) over the frames with a face
definitions.nods_per_min: drops of the head at least 10 degrees below the window's median pitch (ending within 5), per observed minute (assumption: both levels)

eye_methods.caveat: RLDD records the three states of a person as three separate videos, often on another day, device or camera angle. The EAR threshold and the calibration reference come from the alert video and are applied to the other two. The product calibrates at the start of the session it then monitors, a case RLDD does not contain; `calibration_sensitivity` measures what changes when the threshold comes from the scored recording itself.

checks.ear_landmarks_note: share of the frames with a face where the six points of each eye sit where the EAR formula assumes; lids can cross on a fully closed eye

transformation_matrix.note: row-major in Python with the translation in the last column; the browser's flat array is its transpose, so M[2][1] here is m[6] there

pitch_sign.note: correlation between pitch_deg and how far down the nose tip sits between forehead and chin; positive supports PITCH_DOWN_SIGN = +1

dataset.window_rule: 60 s windows every 10 s from the first frame; used when they hold at least 450 frames and a face in at least 80% of them. Every window of the alert video that touches its first 120 s is left out, for training and for scoring: the calibrated alternatives use those seconds, and all four configurations are measured on the same windows. The shipped configuration does not use them for anything.

extraction.note: Per-frame time is FaceLandmarker.detect_for_video in Python on this machine's CPU, measured while several worker processes ran at once. It is not a browser measurement.

drozy_validation.citation: Massoz, Langohr, François & Verly (2016), The ULg Multimodality Drowsiness Database (called DROZY) and Examples of Use, WACV 2016
drozy_validation.licence: DROZY is for research and evaluation only: no commercial use, no redistribution in full or in part, no image shown. The pipeline reads the files and writes aggregate numbers only: no frame, crop or per-frame series, and no recording's KSS or reaction times.
drozy_validation.what: The shipped data/fatigue_model.json applied unchanged to DROZY, whose 14 people the model never saw: nothing is fitted, scaled or chosen on DROZY. Its fatigueScore, PERCLOS alone and the browser's former fixed formula are compared with the mean PVT reaction time and with KSS, on the same windows.

model.trainedOn: UTA-RLDD (Fold1_part1, Fold1_part2, Fold2_part1, Fold2_part2): 3724 windows of 60 s every 10 s from 72 videos of 24 subjects (1047 alert, 1337 low vigilance, 1340 drowsy; self-reported labels)

headline.why: Per recording, because the 36 tests are the only units that do not overlap: windows share 50 of their 60 s and a person's windows share the person, so window counts overstate the evidence. Spearman rather than Pearson, decided before seeing this model's numbers: a test's mean reaction time is pulled up by a few very slow responses, and with 36 points Pearson can be carried by two or three extreme tests (the earlier 3-feature score showed Pearson well above Spearman for that reason). Pearson is reported next to it.

signals.fatigue_score: the shipped model's fatigueScore (data/fatigue_model.json, trained on UTA-RLDD), unchanged
signals.perclos: the model's first feature alone: closed frames / frames with a face, eye closed when mean eyeBlink > 0.5
signals.browser_formula: faceWorker.ts's fixed formula before the model: clamp01(0.6 * perclos + 0.25 * min(1, yawnsPerMin / 4) + 0.15 * clamp01(12 * std(noseY)))

targets.pvt_mean_rt_ms: per window: mean reaction time of the PVT stimuli shown in it (start <= stimulus < start + 60 s); per recording: mean of every reaction time of the test. Reaction time = response time - stimulus time, from pvt-rt/; no stimulus is dropped or capped
targets.kss: KSS (Karolinska Sleepiness Scale; 1 to 9 in DROZY's file, higher = sleepier) is the score DROZY recorded per test. The scale itself is not registered in shared/sources.json: register it before quoting a KSS figure.

dataset.frame_times: DROZY's timestamps/ (elapsed ms), one per decoded frame; frames processed at 15 per second by those times
dataset.window_rule: 60 s windows every 10 s from the first frame, as on RLDD; a window needs at least 450 frames and a face in 80% of them, otherwise it has no score. No window is left out for calibration: the shipped model has none.

limits: Near-infrared Kinect video, 512x424, faces about 65 px wide: not the demo's colour webcam. The numbers do not transfer to it.
14 people and 36 tests: one person can move a per-recording correlation a lot. No interval or p-value is computed.
Windows overlap by 50 s: a window count is not a sample size.
Per recording, the points mix differences between people with changes within a person.
Within one person there are at most 3 distinct KSS values (one per test), and some people have only one or two tests.
The PVT is a reaction test (a mouse click per visual stimulus) taken by people kept awake 28-30 h (`drozy` in shared/sources.json); it is not an astronaut's workload.

KSS (Karolinska Sleepiness Scale; 1 to 9 in DROZY's file, higher = sleepier) is the score DROZY recorded per test. The scale itself is not registered in shared/sources.json: register it before quoting a KSS figure.
